rationale: Executes debug_historian's advisory from 21540c8e round 2 verbatim: the claim 'markup in a removed row cannot reach a visitor, so excluding it from audits is safe' was 'a logical argument, not a measured one — worth a lightweight demand-control test asserting the assembler and this filter share the literal predicate string'. Writing that test MEASURED the claim and REFUTED it: the assembler excludes tombstones with `build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'` (rerender_single_page_action.go ~:870; its own comment explains build_status is NULLABLE — information_schema confirms is_nullable=YES, default 'pending' covers only omitted columns — so a bare inequality would drop NULL-status rows from every assembled page), while toolEligibilityWhere carried a bare `pc.build_status <> 'removed'`. Under SQL three-valued logic a NULL-status row is therefore SERVED by the assembler and INVISIBLE to all three tool audits — the exact inversion of the tombstone defect the filter exists for, and a hole in the round-2 rationale's own 'served-but-excluded is unrepresentable' sentence. Population measured 2026-08-26: ZERO rows fleet-wide with build_status IS NULL, so this closes a LATENT door, not live damage — but nothing constrains the column, so any future explicit NULL write opens it. Fix: align the eligibility predicate to the assembler's NULL-safe spelling (one line; the audited population can only WIDEN, by exactly the NULL rows, currently zero), plus the lockstep scan test the advisory asked for, holding BOTH files to the shared literal with comment lines skipped. Mutation-proven both directions: predicate regressed to `<>` fails both TestToolPopulationQueriesExcludeTombstones and the new test; assembler literal mutated to `!=` fails the new test; restores re-green. DISCLOSED, not changed (per the 2026-07-29 §3 consumers-must-be-told ruling): three further bare-`<>` copies of this clause exist in OTHER consumers — component_selector.go:189, queryresolve/consumers.go:194, check_page_list_stale.go:258 — each caller weighs its own semantics and those belong to their lanes; named in the lane NOTES so their owners can judge the same latency for themselves.

plan.summary: The centralised tool-eligibility tombstone filter (council 21540c8e round 2) spells the exclusion NULL-unsafely (`<>`) while the page assembler it exists to mirror spells it NULL-safely (`IS DISTINCT FROM`), so a NULL build_status row would be served yet invisible to every tool audit. Align the shared predicate to the assembler's spelling and add the lockstep scan test debug_historian's advisory asked for, so neither half of the served-iff-auditable contract can drift alone.

edits.rationale: The one-line predicate alignment: matching the assembler's NULL-safe exclusion makes served-but-unaudited unrepresentable for NULL rows too. All three callers inherit through the centralised predicate with no edits of their own. The comment above the const gains the spelling's rationale and drops the now-conditional 'unrepresentable' phrasing.

edits.rationale: Two parts. (a) The existing scan anchor in TestToolPopulationQueriesExcludeTombstones updates to the new literal so the predicate-carries-it assertion keeps binding. (b) The new lockstep test reads ../rerender_single_page_action.go and tool_eligibility.go, skips comment lines on both files (a source-scan test must never let its own prose satisfy it), and requires the identical NULL-safe literal on both sides — the demand control the advisory named, now also the regression guard for this very fix.

plan.risks: The audited population can only WIDEN, and only by rows with build_status IS NULL — zero exist today, so behaviour is byte-identical on the live fleet until someone writes a NULL. A reviewer should check: (1) that no caller of toolEligibilityWhere RELIES on NULL rows being excluded (the three callers are audit-population queries; none writes); (2) that the lockstep test's comment-skip cannot be satisfied vacuously (both anchors were mutation-proven to fail when either file regresses); (3) whether the three DISCLOSED bare-<> copies in other lanes' files (component_selector.go:189, queryresolve/consumers.go:194, check_page_list_stale.go:258) warrant their own follow-up — deliberately not changed here, different owners, different semantics.
